page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads that require constrained vCPU allocations to optimize software licensing costs. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 system provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features an extensive 260 MB L3 cache, along with Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instructions. Hardware acceleration is non-GPU, but the instance integrates 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

With 768.0 GB of total RAM, the instance delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark results reflect this strong subsystem architecture: uncached large-block read bandwidth reaches 190.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 120.18 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. Geekbench single-core performance scores 2,156.0 alongside strong performance in text processing and image manipulation tasks, while multi-threaded benchmarks such as stress-ng (23,970.13) and PassMark CPU (37,713.62) demonstrate steady mid-tier compute capabilities corresponding to its 24-vCPU quota.

Cost efficiency is centered around core-based database software licensing, where organizations require large memory footprints and local NVMe capacity without incurring the software license overhead associated with a full 96-core deployment. The primary tradeoff lies in raw multi-threaded throughput, which is constrained by the 24 active vCPUs despite the substantial underlying host architecture.

The hardware configuration suits large-footprint in-memory databases, enterprise caching systems such as Redis, in-memory analytical workloads, and data warehouse staging environments that benefit directly from high memory bandwidth and low-latency local NVMe storage.
